cars.variant: GT V6 fastback — 1988 USA factory catalogue, five-speed manual and WS6
cars.specification_market: 1988 USA Fiero GT fastback, standard 2.8-litre V6, selected five-speed manual and WS6 suspension from the original factory full-line catalogue. Count the original 1984–1988 Fiero road family once across years, engines, Coupe/Formula/GT bodies and packages. Not an Indy racing engine, later engine swap, Ferrari replica or unbuilt successor. Preserve factory horsepower/torque without adding missing peak speeds. Stabilizer diameters conflict within the brochure and are not assigned; shared curb-weight range, earlier test times, optional seats and Canadian photo equipment are not selected specifications.
cars.summary: The Fiero is an important American sports-car design experiment, pairing a mid-mounted engine with a spaceframe and replaceable polymer panels. Period recognition and the original tester’s later assessment establish lasting significance despite early shortcomings. The revised 1988 GT represents the whole programme here; it is not claimed to be an outright performance benchmark.

sources.publisher: Pontiac Division, General Motors / XR793 facsimile
sources.title: 1988 Pontiac full-line prestige catalogue — Fiero pages and equipment matrix
sources.source_type: Original manufacturer sales/specification catalogue, hosted scan
sources.notes: 37-page scanned file, 17,859,912 bytes. Full PDF indexes 11 (printed 22–23), 12 (24–25), 31 (62–63) and 32 (64–65) visually read. Vital-specification and Fiero standard-equipment regions enlarged and read. The 37-page thumbnail sheet was navigation only. Matrix confirms GT inherits Formula V6/WS6 and standard manual; the three-speed automatic is optional. GT length differs from Coupe. Rear stabilizer is 22 mm in the technical summary but 23 mm in the standard-equipment list, so no bar diameter is imported. No curb mass assigned from the all-model range.

sources.title: 1984 10Best Cars — original Fiero 2M4 award
sources.notes: Programme-level recognition only: award was for the 1984 four-cylinder 2M4, not this 1988 GT. No earlier specifications imported.

sources.title: Remember the Fiero — John Pearley Huffman, October 2019
sources.source_type: Interview with original road tester, publisher archive
sources.notes: Original tester Rich Ceppos recalls early deficiencies and later improvement. Admission is historical, not a claim of class-leading performance. No earlier times, sales totals or universal first-car claims imported.
